title: Maximum nonlinearity of nonlinear correctors
summary: Determine the exact maximum nonlinearity of an $(n,m,t)$-corrector for every admissible parameter tuple.

formal_statement.body: For every admissible $(n,m,t)$, let $N_{\max}(n,m,t)$ be the largest nonlinearity of an $(n,m,t)$-corrector under the source bias-valuation definition. Determine $N_{\max}(n,m,t)$ by proving a tight upper bound and constructing correctors attaining it for every admissible tuple.

scope.domain: Nonlinear post-processing correctors for true random-number generators with cryptographic nonlinearity objectives
assumptions: Correctors use the source bias-valuation definition
The input dimension, output dimension, and correction order are $(n,m,t)$
The optimization is over the source-admissible corrector family
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result gives a tight maximum for the source corrector family over every admissible $(n,m,t)$.

progress.summary: The source's first open problem asks for the best nonlinearities of $(n,m,t)$-correctors.
